verdict.rationale: Apple's own docs explicitly document MLX support for Metal 4/Neural Accelerators and multi-Mac RDMA training, Core ML/Metal Performance Shaders acceleration, and third-party runtimes like LM Studio benefiting from M5's Neural Accelerators, plus PyTorch-on-Metal backends — strong evidence the vendor stack and MLX target this silicon. Community threads add real-world caveats (153GB/s bandwidth and 32GB RAM cap limiting larger LLM inference) rather than outright contradiction. Missing for 10: explicit llama.cpp support/benchmarks and ONNX Runtime documentation for M5, and independent hands-on confirmation of MLX/Core ML performance claims.
